pk.context: 30 mg oral, steady state, healthy adults

pill.desc: oval, scored tablet, coloured by strength

clues.kinetics: Completely absorbed by mouth, and food slightly raises exposure. About 93% to 95% is protein bound, and it is extensively metabolized, with about 64% of a dose excreted in urine.
clues.substance: A hydrochloride salt whose free base has a molecular weight of 329.4. Its melting point range is 120 to 138 degrees Celsius.
clues.product: An NDA tablet in 10, 20, 30 and 40 mg strengths, taken daily.
clues.safety: Boxed warning for suicidal thoughts and behaviors in pediatric and young adult patients. Contraindicated with MAOIs within 14 days, and with QTc-prolonging drugs that are CYP2D6 substrates.
clues.indication: In adults: major depressive disorder, obsessive compulsive disorder, panic disorder, social anxiety disorder, generalized anxiety disorder and PTSD.
clues.mechanism: Its action is unknown, but is presumed to come from blocking neuronal reuptake of serotonin, potentiating serotonergic activity in the CNS.

tell: Saturable metabolism makes its steady-state exposure about eight times what single-dose data predict.

evidence.pk.halfLifeH: The mean elimination half-life is approximately 21 hours (CV 32%)
evidence.pk.cmax: mean values of C max, T max, C min, and T½ were 61.7 ng/mL (CV 45%)
